tasks.short: Read financial research and assess whether new methods improve existing risk analysis.

steps.what: Define research questions from current model weaknesses and upcoming risk decisions.
Search scholarly databases and regulatory publications through the research service in {OTHER}.
Read selected papers and record methods, assumptions, limitations and validation results.

loop.input: Licensed research papers and a fixed methods-and-limitations checklist.
loop.output: Research findings with page references and quoted support.
loop.check: Require source support for each finding; the specialist checks assumptions, statistics and omitted limitations.
loop.stop: At most eight papers per batch and two passes per paper; unsupported or unreadable passages return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Methods and caveats appear in varied prose, equations and tables; keyword alerts cannot extract their meaning.

steps.what: Compare findings with current models and decide which methods warrant testing.
Approve and file the method review with proposed testing priorities.

tasks.design: Configure source alerts in the research service in {OTHER}, and store a deduplicated reading list in {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares cited research findings; the specialist assesses applicability, and {WORKFLOW} records approval of the method review without changing a production model.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding papers was manageable, but extracting assumptions and comparing methods required specialist reading. Research access and inconsistent paper formats made reusable summaries costly.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing alerts handle discovery. Bounded document extraction can prepare cited notes, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building the review register.
tasks.still_hard: Equations, methodological weaknesses and transfer to the company's exposures still need expert scrutiny. Licensed sources may restrict retrieval or reuse.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when an impressive published result depends on assumptions the company's portfolio cannot meet.

ambition.what: Monthly prioritization of model validation experiments.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time searching and taking notes, and more time comparing methods against actual model weaknesses. They gain a regular route to propose validation experiments; adoption authority remains with the risk model owner.

reach.task: Design reproducible comparisons between candidate risk methods.
reach.learn: Experimental design, leakage checks and out-of-sample validation.

evidence.claim: Research alerts and a structured review register can reduce discovery and filing work.
Cited extraction can assist paper reading, but assessing methodological validity remains specialist work.

assumptions: The company has a small risk team and an identifiable risk model owner.
The starter covers a bounded source catalogue, not exhaustive literature surveillance.
Research uses public or licensed papers rather than employee-level data.
Build ranges cover one research register and review workflow.
unknowns: Which research subscriptions and retrieval rights the company holds.
Whether model reviews already have an approval process.
Which risk methods and validation weaknesses matter most.
Whether existing alerts already remove most search effort.
research_questions: Do extracted limitations match expert reading across prose, tables and equations?
Does the proposed source catalogue miss material developments in the selected risk methods?
new_work: Read passages that extraction cannot support.
Maintain source access, search filters and review questions.
Remove superseded findings from the active reading list.

tasks.short: Help specify, prototype, validate and improve the company's risk management systems.

steps.what: Agree risk decisions, users and control requirements with finance and technical teams.
Export representative exposures and inspect source fields, identifiers and data quality.
Specify mappings, calculations, limits and expected results for the risk analytics software in {OTHER}.
Build spreadsheet prototypes to demonstrate calculations and expected risk outputs.
Configure calculations, limits and views in the risk analytics software in {OTHER}.
Check test results, investigate differences and assess whether controls meet the specification.
Approve release scope and accept documented residual risks.
Update operating instructions and record approved changes for users.

tasks.design: Use {DATA_PLATFORM} to collect reconciled exposures from {ERP}, {BANK} and the risk analytics software in {OTHER}, then generate prototypes and regression results from versioned specifications. Configure supported controls in {OTHER}, expose results in {BI}, and use {WORKFLOW} to require release approval before production changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source mappings, spreadsheet prototypes and system configuration were maintained separately. Building reliable integration and regression checks required scarce engineering time.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connectors, fixtures and calculation modules. Existing configuration remains the cheapest route where the risk analytics software in {OTHER} already supports the requirement.
tasks.still_hard: Exposure definitions, model validity and acceptable residual risk remain judgement calls. Legacy interfaces, independent validation and release governance can dominate delivery time.
tasks.human_edge: Translate financial risk into useful controls and recognize when passing technical tests still leaves an unsafe decision process.

ambition.what: A pre-release risk control check for finance system changes.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time rebuilding prototypes and documenting test results, and more time challenging assumptions and investigating failures. They can gain authority to require validation evidence before a proposed risk-system release; release approval remains with the finance manager.

reach.task: Build reconciled risk dashboards with clear exposure definitions.
reach.learn: Data lineage, semantic definitions and reconciliation design.

reach.task: Test access controls and evidence supporting risk-system changes.
reach.learn: Control testing, segregation of duties and audit evidence.

evidence.claim: Rules, configuration and deterministic regression checks suit specified financial calculations and limits.
DataSnipper supports evidence-linked financial checks with team review and sign-off; it does not establish risk-model validity.
The digest's cash-waterfall benchmark illustrates why generated financial calculations need independent expected results.

assumptions: The first build covers one exposure domain and an existing risk analytics system.
The risk analytics software in {OTHER} supports configuration and a separate test environment.
Generated prototypes and configuration remain in testing until release approval.
The estimates cover a starter control framework, not replacement of a core risk platform.
GDPR applies to personal data; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Natural-person credit decisions would require a separate GDPR and EU AI Act assessment.
unknowns: Available interfaces, test environments and configuration capabilities.
Who owns exposure definitions and production release authority.
Whether models require independent validation or sector-specific approval.
Whether employee data or natural-person credit assessments are in scope.
research_questions: Can deterministic calculations reproduce approved benchmark cases across currencies, dates and missing values?
Which requirements can be configured without custom code?
Can changes be traced from specification through testing to production release?
new_work: Maintain mappings, expected results and regression fixtures.
Investigate reconciliation failures and changed source schemas.
Review generated configuration and operating instructions.
Maintain access permissions, release records and rollback procedures.

tasks.short: Assess how new products or processes affect environmental exposure, long-term growth and profitability.

steps.what: Clarify the proposed product or process, investment horizon and decision required.
Read technical studies and identify energy, emissions, resource use and environmental constraints.

loop.input: Technical studies and supplier specifications for one proposed product or process.
loop.output: Environmental impact register with units, scope, uncertainty and source references.
loop.check: Validate units and identifiers; require a source for every claim and specialist review of boundaries and omissions.
loop.stop: At most twelve documents and two passes per document; ambiguous measurements or conflicting scopes become explicit exceptions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Environmental boundaries, qualifications and claimed impacts are expressed inconsistently in technical prose.

steps.what: Gather current costs, volumes and operational baselines for financial comparison.
Agree plausible demand, resource-price, regulatory and disruption scenarios with relevant specialists.
Calculate scenario cash flows, profitability and sensitivity to environmental exposure.
Assess uncertainties, trade-offs and conditions that could change the investment recommendation.
Assemble the assessment pack with assumptions, scenario tables and recommendation.
Discuss the assessment and approve, defer or reject the proposed investment.

tasks.design: A scoped intake in {WORKFLOW} collects the proposal, while bounded extraction turns studies in {DOCS} into a cited environmental impact register. Deterministic jobs on {DATA_PLATFORM} join baselines from {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, calculate agreed scenarios and feed {BI}; a template generates the assessment pack for the investment committee.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical studies, operating measurements and financial models used different boundaries and units. Each assessment required manual collection, spreadsheet assembly and report formatting.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can prepare source-linked impact records, and AI-assisted coding makes reusable unit checks and scenario calculators cheaper to build. These tools do not resolve uncertain environmental or commercial assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier claims may lack comparable evidence. Long-term demand, regulation, physical hazards and environmental effects have uncertain causal links to profit.
tasks.human_edge: Choose credible scenarios, challenge environmental claims and explain trade-offs without presenting uncertain forecasts as facts.

ambition.what: Early environmental-financial screening for product development teams.

tasks.altitude: The specialist can join proposal reviews earlier because data collection and scenario assembly take less time. They can gain authority to request evidence or sensitivity analysis before committee review; investment approval remains with the committee.

reach.task: Translate resource-use scenarios into operating budgets.
reach.learn: Budget drivers, forecast horizons and cost allocation.

reach.task: Estimate lifecycle costs of proposed products and processes.
reach.learn: Engineering quantities, lifecycle boundaries and uncertainty ranges.

evidence.claim: Cytora structures underwriting submissions; this supports document-extraction feasibility, not environmental forecasting accuracy.
Versioned assumptions and deterministic scenario calculations can replace repeated spreadsheet assembly.
Environmental impacts must be connected to financial outcomes through explicit, reviewable assumptions.

assumptions: The assessment supports an internal investment decision rather than certifying environmental claims.
A technical or environmental specialist supplies or reviews environmental evidence.
The first build covers one product or process category with reusable scenario formulas.
The extraction register preserves uncertainty and does not fill missing measurements with invented values.
GDPR applies if supplied records contain personal data; consultation requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Which environmental measurements and supplier evidence are available.
Who validates environmental boundaries and technical assumptions.
Which investment horizons and approval thresholds apply.
Whether operational data can be linked to the proposed process.
Whether the change uses employee-level data or triggers national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can studies be compared without mixing different lifecycle boundaries or measurement units?
Which assumptions most strongly change the investment recommendation?
How well do historical resource-use and cost scenarios match observed outcomes?
new_work: Review extracted units, boundaries and unsupported supplier claims.
Maintain scenario assumptions and financial formulas.
Investigate missing or conflicting environmental measurements.
Compare realized costs and impacts with the original assessment.

tasks.short: Prepare financial contingency plans, test them and obtain approval for emergency responses.

steps.what: Collect current exposures, cash positions and existing emergency documents.
Identify funding constraints, critical dependencies, responsible roles and recovery requirements.

loop.input: Existing plans, funding agreements and service agreements for one financial contingency domain.
loop.output: Dependency inventory and response constraints with clause or page references.
loop.check: Require cited support, distinguish obligations from options, and have owners confirm critical dependencies.
loop.stop: At most fifteen documents and two passes per document; conflicts or unclear obligations return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dependencies and restrictions are distributed across varied contracts and narrative plans.

steps.what: Run agreed emergency scenarios and calculate liquidity needs, losses and limit breaches.
Agree response priorities, escalation thresholds, owners and fallback actions.
Write the contingency plan, checklists and contact annex.
Rehearse emergency scenarios and record gaps in the proposed response.
Approve the revised plan and its delegated emergency authorities.
Distribute the approved plan and schedule ownership checks and future exercises.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile exposures from {ERP} and {BANK}, while bounded extraction prepares cited constraints from {DOCS} and {CLM}. Deterministic stress calculations feed {BI}, and a template produces the plan from a human-agreed response matrix. {WORKFLOW} distributes only approved versions and schedules checks; emergency payments, trades and external communications retain their own authorization rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were assembled from scattered contracts, cash models and contact lists. Keeping every annex current required repeated manual work, while crisis priorities remained difficult to formalize.
tasks.enabler_now: Integrations, deterministic scenario tools and template generation can now be built and maintained with less engineering effort. Bounded extraction helps find documented constraints without taking emergency decisions.
tasks.still_hard: A documented funding option may not be available during a real crisis. Correlated failures, changing counterparties and practical execution capacity still require rehearsals and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose workable priorities under pressure and secure commitment from the people expected to execute the response.

ambition.what: Monthly reassessment of liquidity contingency triggers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time refreshing annexes and rerunning stress spreadsheets, and more time rehearsing failures and challenging response capacity. They can gain authority to call a readiness review when an approved trigger changes; emergency financial authority remains explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Assess emergency liquidity sources and funding constraints.
reach.learn: Cash forecasting, facility conditions and payment authorization.

reach.task: Review emergency obligations and delegated authority.
reach.learn: Escalation duties, evidence retention and applicable national rules.

evidence.claim: Deterministic stress calculations and templates can automate plan preparation without automating emergency judgement.
Moody's Credit Memo drafts from financial inputs, deal documents and templates; this supports drafting feasibility, not contingency-plan effectiveness.
Tabletop exercises reveal execution gaps that document completeness checks cannot establish.

assumptions: The starter covers financial contingencies such as liquidity stress, counterparty failure or banking disruption.
Stress assumptions are agreed by people and versioned before calculations run.
The response matrix records actions in structured fields suitable for template generation.
Existing limits and bank mandates govern emergency execution.
Contact rosters use necessary personal data with controlled access under GDPR.
Employee consultation is included where applicable under national rules.
unknowns: Which contingency scenarios and recovery objectives are already approved.
Whether funding agreements and bank mandates are current and accessible.
Who can authorize emergency payments, borrowing and external communications.
Whether critical contacts and fallback channels are tested.
Which national consultation or sector-specific requirements apply.
research_questions: Do stress calculations reproduce approved historical or benchmark scenarios?
Can each response action be executed within its stated time and authority limits?
Do exercises expose dependencies missing from the document-derived inventory?
new_work: Review extracted contractual constraints and unresolved conflicts.
Maintain stress assumptions, contact rosters and response ownership.
Check funding availability and changed bank mandates.
Run exercises and close documented readiness gaps.
Maintain approval history and remove obsolete plan versions.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward model challenge, investment uncertainty and operational readiness as collection, calculations and paperwork shrink. The specialist can gain authority to request validation evidence and convene readiness reviews; financial commitments and risk acceptance remain with designated approvers.
reach: Work with Data Scientists on reproducible model comparisons.
Work with Business Intelligence Analysts on reconciled exposure definitions.
Work with Budget Analysts and Cost Estimators on environmental-financial scenarios.
Work with Treasurers and Controllers on executable liquidity responses.
Work with Compliance Officers on obligations and delegated authority.
skills_to_grow: Deterministic calculation specification and independent test design.
Source verification for bounded document extraction.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring risk decision service that connects method reviews, tested system changes, early investment screening and liquidity readiness. Its value comes from better evidence and earlier challenge, with explicit human authority over consequential decisions.
